sanskrit: teṣāṃ caivāpavargāya mārgaṃ paśyāmi nāṇḍaja tato 'yaṃ jīvitatyāge dṛṣṭo mārgo mayātmanaḥ
english: I see no way to bring those to an end, O bird. Therefore this is the path I have found for myself — to abandon life itself.

sanskrit: naiva me 'sti dhanaṃ kiṃ cin na dhanenānvitaḥ suhṛt na cārthenāpi mahatā śakyam etad vyapohitum
english: I have no wealth at all, nor any friend possessed of wealth; nor can this debt be discharged even by a great sum.

sanskrit: nārada uvāca evaṃ bahu ca dīnaṃ ca bruvāṇaṃ gālavaṃ tadā pratyuvāca vrajann eva prahasan vinatātmajaḥ
english: Nārada said: While Gālava was speaking thus at length and in misery, the son of Vinatā, even as he flew on, laughed and replied.

sanskrit: nātiprajño 'si viprarṣe yo ''tmānaṃ tyaktum icchasi na cāpi kṛtrimaḥ kālaḥ kālo hi parameśvaraḥ
english: You are not very wise, O brahmin-seer, that you wish to cast away your life. Moreover, one must not force time; for Time is the supreme lord.

sanskrit: kim ahaṃ pūrvam eveha bhavatā nābhicoditaḥ upāyo 'tra mahān asti yenaitad upapadyate
english: Why did you not prompt me about this matter from the very beginning? There is a great means by which this can be accomplished.

sanskrit: tad eṣa ṛṣabho nāma parvataḥ sāgarorasi atra viśramya bhuktvā ca nivartiṣyāva gālava
english: There on the shore of the ocean is a mountain named Ṛṣabha. Let us rest and eat there, and then we shall turn our course, O Gālava.

sanskrit: nārada uvāca ṛṣabhasya tataḥ śṛṅge nipatya dvijapakṣiṇau śāṇḍilīṃ brāhmaṇīṃ tatra dadṛśāte taponvitām
english: Nārada said: The two — the brahmin and the bird — then alighted on the peak of Ṛṣabha, and there they saw the brahmin woman Śāṇḍilī, endowed with austerity.

sanskrit: abhivādya suparṇas tu gālavaś cābhipūjya tām tayā ca svāgatenoktau viṣṭare saṃniṣīdatuḥ
english: Suparṇa saluted her and Gālava honoured her respectfully; and welcomed by her, the two sat down upon seats she offered.

sanskrit: siddham annaṃ tayā kṣipraṃ balimantropabṛṃhitam bhuktvā tṛptāv ubhau bhūmau suptau tāv annamohitau
english: She quickly prepared food, enriched with sacred offerings and mantras; and having eaten and become satisfied, both of them lay down on the ground, overcome by the food.

sanskrit: muhūrtāt pratibuddhas tu suparṇo gamanepsayā atha bhraṣṭatanūjāṅgam ātmānaṃ dadṛśe khagaḥ
english: After a while Suparṇa awoke, wishing to depart; but then the bird found himself stripped of the limbs of his body.

sanskrit: māṃsapiṇḍopamo 'bhūt sa mukhapādānvitaḥ khagaḥ gālavas taṃ tathā dṛṣṭvā viṣaṇṇaḥ paryapṛcchata
english: The bird had become like a lump of flesh, retaining only his beak and feet. Gālava, seeing him in that state, was distressed and questioned him.

sanskrit: kim idaṃ bhavatā prāptam ihāgamanajaṃ phalam vāso 'yam iha kālaṃ tu kiyantaṃ nau bhaviṣyati
english: What fruit of coming here has befallen you? And for how long shall we have to remain here?

sanskrit: kiṃ nu te manasā dhyātam aśubhaṃ dharmadūṣaṇam na hy ayaṃ bhavataḥ svalpo vyabhicāro bhaviṣyati
english: What inauspicious and dharma-violating thought did you harbour in your mind? For this transgression of yours is surely not a trifling one.

sanskrit: suparṇo 'thābravīd vipraṃ pradhyātaṃ vai mayā dvija imāṃ siddhām ito netuṃ tatra yatra prajāpatiḥ
english: Suparṇa then said to the brahmin: I had indeed meditated, O brahmin, on carrying this perfected woman away from here to the place where Prajāpati dwells.

sanskrit: yatra devo mahādevo yatra viṣṇuḥ sanātanaḥ yatra dharmaś ca yajñaś ca tatreyaṃ nivased iti
english: Where the god Mahādeva is, where eternal Viṣṇu is, where Dharma and Sacrifice dwell — there, I thought, let her reside.

sanskrit: so 'haṃ bhagavatīṃ yāce praṇataḥ priyakāmyayā mayaitan nāma pradhyātaṃ manasā śocatā kila
english: Therefore I bow and beg the gracious lady with a mind well disposed; indeed my mind pondered this wish, though I am now filled with remorse.

sanskrit: tad evaṃ bahumānāt te mayehānīpsitaṃ kṛtam sukṛtaṃ duṣkṛtaṃ vā tvaṃ māhātmyāt kṣantum arhasi
english: Out of deep reverence for you I here sought what was not to be sought; whether it was well done or ill done, by your great-souled grace please forgive it.

sanskrit: sā tau tadābravīt tuṣṭā patagendradvijarṣabhau na bhetavyaṃ suparṇo 'si suparṇa tyaja saṃbhramam
english: Pleased, she then said to the two — the lord of birds and the best of brahmins: Fear not; you are Suparṇa — O Suparṇa, set aside your agitation.

sanskrit: ninditāsmi tvayā vatsa na ca nindāṃ kṣamāmy aham lokebhyaḥ sa paribhraśyed yo māṃ nindeta pāpakṛt
english: You have reproached me, my child, and I do not lightly forgive reproach; the sinful one who disparages me falls from the worlds.

sanskrit: hīnayālakṣaṇaiḥ sarvais tathāninditayā mayā ācāraṃ pratigṛhṇantyā siddhiḥ prāpteyam uttamā
english: Though lacking in all auspicious marks, and not censured by me, having accepted righteous conduct, I have attained this supreme perfection.

sanskrit: ācārāl labhate dharmam ācārāl labhate dhanam ācārāc chriyam āpnoti ācāro hanty alakṣaṇam
english: From right conduct one gains dharma; from right conduct one gains wealth; through right conduct one attains prosperity; right conduct destroys inauspiciousness.

sanskrit: tadāyuṣman khagapate yatheṣṭaṃ gamyatām itaḥ na ca te garhaṇīyāpi garhitavyāḥ striyaḥ kva cit
english: Therefore, O long-lived lord of birds, go from here as you wish. And women who are worthy of blame should nonetheless never be blamed by you.

sanskrit: bhavitāsi yathāpūrvaṃ balavīryasamanvitaḥ babhūvatus tatas tasya pakṣau draviṇavattarau
english: You shall be as before, endowed with strength and valour. Thereupon his wings became even more splendid than before.

sanskrit: anujñātaś ca śāṇḍilyā yathāgatam upāgamat naiva cāsādayām āsa tathārūpāṃs turaṃgamān
english: Permitted by Śāṇḍilī, he set out as he had come; yet he was unable to find horses of that description.

sanskrit: viśvāmitro 'tha taṃ dṛṣṭvā gālavaṃ cādhvani sthitam uvāca vadatāṃ śreṣṭho vainateyasya saṃnidhau
english: Viśvāmitra then, seeing Gālava standing on the road in the presence of the son of Vinatā, spoke — the foremost of the eloquent.

sanskrit: yas tvayā svayam evārthaḥ pratijñāto mama dvija tasya kālo 'pavargasya yathā vā manyate bhavān
english: The matter which you yourself promised me, O brahmin — the time for its fulfillment has come, or so you may reckon.

sanskrit: pratīkṣiṣyāmy ahaṃ kālam etāvantaṃ tathā param yathā saṃsidhyate vipra sa mārgas tu niśamyatām
english: I shall wait this much time and a little beyond, as the means for accomplishing it may be found, O brahmin. That course of action, however, should be heard now.

sanskrit: suparṇo 'thābravīd dīnaṃ gālavaṃ bhṛśaduḥkhitam pratyakṣaṃ khalv idānīṃ me viśvāmitro yad uktavān
english: Suparṇa then said to the wretched and deeply distressed Gālava: What Viśvāmitra said is now plainly before me.

sanskrit: tad āgaccha dvijaśreṣṭha mantrayiṣyāva gālava nādattvā gurave śakyaṃ kṛtsnam arthaṃ tvayāsitum
english: So come, O best of brahmins, let us deliberate together, O Gālava; it is not possible for you to live without having given the guru-gift in full.

sanskrit: nārada uvāca athāha gālavaṃ dīnaṃ suparṇaḥ patatāṃ varaḥ nirmitaṃ vahninā bhūmau vāyunā vaidhitaṃ tathā yasmād dhiraṇmayaṃ sarvaṃ hiraṇyaṃ tena cocyate
english: Nārada said: Then the best of birds addressed the wretched Gālava: What was fashioned by fire on the earth and ordered by the wind — because everything is made of gold-stuff, it is called hiraṇya.

sanskrit: dhatte dhārayate cedam etasmāt kāraṇād dhanam tad etat triṣu lokeṣu dhanaṃ tiṣṭhati śāśvatam
english: It bears and sustains everything; for that reason it is called wealth (dhana). This wealth abides eternally in the three worlds.

sanskrit: nityaṃ proṣṭhapadābhyāṃ ca śukre dhanapatau tathā manuṣyebhyaḥ samādatte śukraś cittārjitaṃ dhanam
english: Ever through the two Proṣṭhapada stars and through Śukra the lord of wealth, Śukra takes from men the wealth earned by the mind.

sanskrit: ajaikapādahirbudhnyai rakṣyate dhanadena ca evaṃ na śakyate labdhum alabdhavyaṃ dvijarṣabha
english: It is guarded by Ajaikapāda, Ahirbudhnya, and Dhanada; thus what is not destined to be obtained cannot be obtained, O best of brahmins.

sanskrit: ṛte ca dhanam aśvānāṃ nāvāptir vidyate tava arthaṃ yācātra rājānaṃ kaṃ cid rājarṣivaṃśajam apīḍya rājā paurān hi yo nau kuryāt kṛtārthinau
english: Apart from the wealth of horses there is no fulfillment for you. Beg here from some king born of royal-seer lineage — a king who, without oppressing his people, would make both of us successful in our aim.

sanskrit: asti somānvavāye me jātaḥ kaś cin nṛpaḥ sakhā abhigacchāvahe taṃ vai tasyāsti vibhavo bhuvi
english: There is in the lunar lineage a certain king, a friend of mine. Let us go to him; he has great prosperity on earth.

sanskrit: yayātir nāma rājarṣir nāhuṣaḥ satyavikramaḥ sa dāsyati mayā cokto bhavatā cārthitaḥ svayam
english: He is Yayāti, the royal seer, son of Nahuṣa, true in valour; spoken to by me and personally petitioned by you, he will give.

sanskrit: vibhavaś cāsya sumahān āsīd dhanapater iva evaṃ sa tu dhanaṃ vidvān dānenaiva vyaśodhayat
english: His prosperity had been exceedingly great, like that of the lord of wealth; knowing the nature of wealth, he purified himself through charity alone.

sanskrit: tathā tau kathayantau ca cintayantau ca yat kṣamam pratiṣṭhāne narapatiṃ yayātiṃ pratyupasthitau
english: Thus deliberating and reflecting on what was proper, the two presented themselves at the abode of the lord of men, Yayāti.

sanskrit: pratigṛhya ca satkāram arghādiṃ bhojanaṃ varam pṛṣṭaś cāgamane hetum uvāca vinatāsutaḥ
english: Having received the hospitality of welcome-gift and excellent food, and being asked the reason for coming, the son of Vinatā spoke.

sanskrit: ayaṃ me nāhuṣa sakhā gālavas tapaso nidhiḥ viśvāmitrasya śiṣyo 'bhūd varṣāṇy ayutaśo nṛpa
english: This is my friend, O son of Nahuṣa — Gālava, a treasury of austerity; he was the disciple of Viśvāmitra for tens of thousands of years, O king.

sanskrit: so 'yaṃ tenābhyanujñāta upakārepsayā dvijaḥ tam āha bhagavān kāṃ te dadāni gurudakṣiṇām
english: Released by him and wishing to offer something in return, this brahmin asked the venerable one: What guru-gift shall I give you?

sanskrit: asakṛt tena coktena kiṃ cid āgatamanyunā ayam uktaḥ prayaccheti jānatā vibhavaṃ laghu
english: Being asked repeatedly by him who was slightly angered, and knowing his own modest means, he was told: Give this.

sanskrit: ekataḥśyāmakarṇānāṃ śubhrāṇāṃ śuddhajanmanām aṣṭau śatāni me dehi hayānāṃ candravarcasām
english: Give me eight hundred horses of uniform dark ear, white-bodied, of pure birth, brilliant as the moon.

sanskrit: gurvartho dīyatām eṣa yadi gālava manyase ity evam āha sakrodho viśvāmitras tapodhanaḥ
english: Let this be given as the guru-gift, if you concur, O Gālava — thus spoke Viśvāmitra, the wealth of whose power lay in austerity, with some anger.

sanskrit: so 'yaṃ śokena mahatā tapyamāno dvijarṣabhaḥ aśaktaḥ pratikartuṃ tad bhavantaṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ
english: This best of brahmins, scorched by great grief and unable to fulfil it, has come to you for refuge.

sanskrit: pratigṛhya naravyāghra tvatto bhikṣāṃ gatavyathaḥ kṛtvāpavargaṃ gurave cariṣyati mahat tapaḥ
english: Having received alms from you, O tiger among men, freed from distress, having discharged the debt to his guru, he shall practise great austerity.

sanskrit: tapasaḥ saṃvibhāgena bhavantam api yokṣyate svena rājarṣitapasā pūrṇaṃ tvāṃ pūrayiṣyati
english: Through a share of his austerity he will connect you as well; with his own austerity befitting a royal seer he will fill you who are already full.

sanskrit: yāvanti romāṇi haye bhavanti hi nareśvara tāvato vājidā lokān prāpnuvanti mahīpate
english: As many hairs as there are on a horse, O lord of men, so many worlds do the givers of horses attain, O lord of the earth.

sanskrit: pātraṃ pratigrahasyāyaṃ dātuṃ pātraṃ tathā bhavān śaṅkhe kṣīram ivāsaktaṃ bhavatv etat tathopamam
english: He is the worthy vessel for receiving, and you likewise are the worthy vessel for giving; let this be like milk poured into a conch — well fitted in comparison.

sanskrit: nārada uvāca evam uktaḥ suparṇena tathyaṃ vacanam uttamam vimṛśyāvahito rājā niścitya ca punaḥ punaḥ
english: Nārada said: Thus addressed by Suparṇa with true and excellent words, the king, attentive and having deliberated again and again, resolved.

sanskrit: yaṣṭā kratusahasrāṇāṃ dātā dānapatiḥ prabhuḥ yayātir vatsakāśīśa idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Yayāti, performer of thousands of sacrifices, lord of giving, the master, the ruler of Vatsakā and Kāśī, spoke these words.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā priyasakhaṃ tārkṣyaṃ gālavaṃ ca dvijarṣabham nidarśanaṃ ca tapaso bhikṣāṃ ślāghyāṃ ca kīrtitām
english: Having seen Tārkṣya my dear friend, and Gālava the best of brahmins, and the manifest proof of austerity, and the praiseworthy begging mission proclaimed —

sanskrit: atītya ca nṛpān anyān ādityakulasaṃbhavān matsakāśam anuprāptāv etau buddhim avekṣya ca
english: And having bypassed other kings born of the solar lineage, these two have come to my presence — weighing my judgment —

sanskrit: adya me saphalaṃ janma tāritaṃ cādya me kulam adyāyaṃ tārito deśo mama tārkṣya tvayānagha
english: Today my birth is fulfilled; today my lineage is redeemed; today this my country is redeemed by you, O sinless Tārkṣya.

sanskrit: vaktum icchāmi tu sakhe yathā jānāsi māṃ purā na tathā vittavān asmi kṣīṇaṃ vittaṃ hi me sakhe
english: Yet I wish to speak, my friend, as you know me from before — I am not as wealthy as I was; my wealth is depleted, O friend.

sanskrit: na ca śakto 'smi te kartuṃ mogham āgamanaṃ khaga na cāśām asya viprarṣer vitathāṃ kartum utsahe
english: I am not able to make your coming here in vain, O bird; nor do I have the heart to make the hope of this brahmin-seer empty.

sanskrit: tat tu dāsyāmi yat kāryam idaṃ saṃpādayiṣyati abhigamya hatāśo hi nivṛtto dahate kulam
english: Yet I will give what will accomplish this task; for one who goes to a patron and returns with hope destroyed burns down the lineage.

sanskrit: nātaḥ paraṃ vainateya kiṃ cit pāpiṣṭham ucyate yathāśānāśanaṃ loke dehi nāstīti vā vacaḥ
english: Nothing more sinful than this is spoken of, O son of Vinatā — as the word 'give' is the destroyer of expectation in the world, so is the word 'there is not.'

sanskrit: hatāśo hy akṛtārthaḥ san hataḥ saṃbhāvito naraḥ hinasti tasya putrāṃś ca pautrāṃś cākurvato 'rthinām
english: For a respected man, if he fails to act and leaves a petitioner with dashed hopes and unaccomplished aim, destroys his sons and grandsons.

sanskrit: tasmāc caturṇāṃ vaṃśānāṃ sthāpayitrī sutā mama iyaṃ surasutaprakhyā sarvadharmopacāyinī
english: Therefore my daughter — like the daughter of the gods, enriching all dharma, the establisher of four lineages — this one I offer.

sanskrit: sadā devamanuṣyāṇām asurāṇāṃ ca gālava kāṅkṣitā rūpato bālā sutā me pratigṛhyatām
english: Ever desired by gods, men, and asuras alike for her beauty, O Gālava — let this young daughter of mine be accepted.

sanskrit: asyāḥ śulkaṃ pradāsyanti nṛpā rājyam api dhruvam kiṃ punaḥ śyāmakarṇānāṃ hayānāṃ dve catuḥśate
english: Kings will give even their kingdoms as her bride-price without doubt; how much more will they give two hundred of the dark-eared horses?

sanskrit: sa bhavān pratigṛhṇātu mamemāṃ mādhavīṃ sutām ahaṃ dauhitravān syāṃ vai vara eṣa mama prabho
english: You, sir, please accept this my daughter Mādhavī; I shall become possessed of grandsons — that indeed is my boon, O lord.

sanskrit: pratigṛhya ca tāṃ kanyāṃ gālavaḥ saha pakṣiṇā punar drakṣyāva ity uktvā pratasthe saha kanyayā
english: Gālava accepted that maiden, and with the bird said 'We shall meet again,' then set out with the maiden.

sanskrit: upalabdham idaṃ dvāram aśvānām iti cāṇḍajaḥ uktvā gālavam āpṛcchya jagāma bhavanaṃ svakam
english: 'This door to the horses has been found,' said the egg-born one; and bidding farewell to Gālava, he went to his own home.

sanskrit: gate patagarāje tu gālavaḥ saha kanyayā cintayānaḥ kṣamaṃ dāne rājñāṃ vai śulkato 'gamat
english: When the lord of birds had gone, Gālava, together with the maiden, reflecting on who among kings was capable of giving the bride-price, set out.

sanskrit: so 'gacchan manasekṣvākuṃ haryaśvaṃ rājasattamam ayodhyāyāṃ mahāvīryaṃ caturaṅgabalānvitam
english: He went mentally toward Haryaśva of the Ikṣvāku line, the best of kings, of great valour, endowed with a four-fold army at Ayodhyā.

sanskrit: kośadhānyabalopetaṃ priyapauraṃ dvijapriyam prajābhikāmaṃ śāmyantaṃ kurvāṇaṃ tapa uttamam
english: Possessed of treasury, grain, and military strength, beloved by his citizens, dear to brahmins, eager to protect his subjects, practicing supreme austerity in tranquility.

sanskrit: tam upāgamya vipraḥ sa haryaśvaṃ gālavo 'bravīt kanyeyaṃ mama rājendra prasavaiḥ kulavardhinī
english: Approaching him, Gālava the brahmin said to Haryaśva: O king of kings, this is my maiden — she who through her offspring increases dynasties.

sanskrit: iyaṃ śulkena bhāryārthe haryaśva pratigṛhyatām śulkaṃ te kīrtayiṣyāmi tac chrutvā saṃpradhāryatām
english: Accept her, O Haryaśva, as a wife in exchange for bride-price. I shall declare the bride-price to you; hear it and then deliberate.

sanskrit: nārada uvāca haryaśvas tv abravīd rājā vicintya bahudhā tataḥ dīrgham uṣṇaṃ ca niḥśvasya prajāhetor nṛpottamaḥ
english: Nārada said: Then King Haryaśva, having pondered deeply and heaving a long hot sigh for the sake of progeny — that best of kings — spoke.

sanskrit: unnateṣūnnatā ṣaṭsu sūkṣmā sūkṣmeṣu saptasu gambhīrā triṣu gambhīreṣv iyaṃ raktā ca pañcasu
english: Elevated among the six elevated things; subtle among the seven subtle things; deep among the three deep things; and red in five respects — she has all this.

sanskrit: bahudevāsurālokā bahugandharvadarśanā bahulakṣaṇasaṃpannā bahuprasavadhāriṇī
english: Beheld by many gods and asuras, seen by many gandharvas, endowed with many auspicious marks, bearing the capacity for many births.

sanskrit: samartheyaṃ janayituṃ cakravartinam ātmajam brūhi śulkaṃ dvijaśreṣṭha samīkṣya vibhavaṃ mama
english: She is capable of giving birth to a world-ruling son. Tell me the bride-price, O best of brahmins, having considered my resources.

sanskrit: gālava uvāca ekataḥśyāmakarṇānāṃ śatāny aṣṭau dadasva me hayānāṃ candraśubhrāṇāṃ deśajānāṃ vapuṣmatām
english: Gālava said: Give me eight hundred horses of uniform dark ear, moon-white, born of the proper country, of handsome form.

sanskrit: tatas tava bhavitrīyaṃ putrāṇāṃ jananī śubhā araṇīva hutāśānāṃ yonir āyatalocanā
english: Then she will be yours — the auspicious mother of sons, the womb of your fires like the araṇī is the source of the sacrificial flame, the large-eyed one.

sanskrit: nārada uvāca etac chrutvā vaco rājā haryaśvaḥ kāmamohitaḥ uvāca gālavaṃ dīno rājarṣir ṛṣisattamam
english: Nārada said: Hearing these words, King Haryaśva, bewildered by desire, the royal seer spoke in distress to Gālava the best of sages.

sanskrit: dve me śate saṃnihite hayānāṃ yad vidhās tava eṣṭavyāḥ śataśas tv anye caranti mama vājinaḥ
english: Two hundred horses of the kind you describe are at hand for me; other horses of mine roam by the hundreds.

sanskrit: so 'ham ekam apatyaṃ vai janayiṣyāmi gālava asyām etaṃ bhavān kāmaṃ saṃpādayatu me varam
english: I shall beget a single offspring upon her, O Gālava; let you fulfil this desire of mine as a boon.

sanskrit: etac chrutvā tu sā kanyā gālavaṃ vākyam abravīt mama datto varaḥ kaś cit kena cid brahmavādinā
english: Hearing this, the maiden spoke these words to Gālava: A certain boon was granted to me by a speaker of brahman —
